questions.question: What is the main purpose of a powertrain?
options: Transfer engine power to the drive wheels or tracks
questions.explanation: The powertrain moves power from the engine to the ground. It includes components such as clutch, transmission, driveline, axle, and final drive. Its job is to provide usable torque and speed.

questions.category: I2 — Service, diagnose, and repair clutches
questions.question: A clutch is used to:
options: Connect and disconnect engine power from the transmission
questions.explanation: The clutch controls power flow between engine and transmission. It allows starting, stopping, and gear changes. A slipping or dragging clutch affects machine operation.

questions.category: I3 — Service, diagnose, and repair manual transmissions
questions.question: A manual transmission uses gears to change:
questions.explanation: Different gear ratios change output speed and torque. Low gears provide more torque. High gears provide more speed.

questions.category: I4 — Service, diagnose, and repair automated transmissions
questions.question: An automated manual transmission shifts using:
questions.explanation: Automated transmissions use electronic control of shifting. Actuators may operate the clutch and shift rails. Sensors provide position and speed data.

questions.category: I5 — Automatic transmissions and torque converters
questions.question: An automatic transmission uses hydraulic pressure to:
questions.explanation: Automatic transmissions use pressurized fluid for control. Clutches and bands are applied by hydraulic pressure. Low pressure causes slipping or no movement.
